title: Ops Tactician: Weekly Playback — Apr 12–18 2027
content:
Purpose: quick internal playback from the private-deploys week (Apr 12–18). Focus areas: two active installs, one escalated network anomaly, preflight checklist gaps, and short-term mitigations for a recurring KV cache OOM pattern.

Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Ravi Kapoor (network lead), Sofia Martinez (field eng), Liam O'Neill (SRE on-call), Anya Petrov (customer success rep), plus notes from on-call shift.

Summary of active installs:
- Project: Horizon Analytics (VPC on-prem hybrid) — Day 3 of install. Status: partial traffic, model load consistent but intermittent job failures when prefix cache warms under burst traffic.
  - Symptom: model inference processes crash with OOM during initial ramp (observed 3x between 04/14 09:00–16:00).
  - Immediate mitigation applied: reduced concurrent worker count (from 8 -> 4) and enabled aggressive KV-cache eviction policy for warmup window.
  - Owner: Sofia Martinez.
  - Jira: PD-3421 (root-cause and long-term fix).

- Project: Meridian Financials (VPC-only, corporate datacenter) — Day 1 handoff. Status: blocked on network egress policies and DNS split-horizon mismatch.
  - Symptom: control-plane agent cannot reach package mirror (internal endpoint resolves to prod cloud IPs due to split-horizon difference).
  - Current action: Ravi to coordinate with customer netops to add static resolver entry for mirror and document fallback mirror option in preflight.
  - Owner: Ravi Kapoor.
  - Jira: PD-3487 (networking + preflight action).

Escalations and incidents:
- DNS split-horizon (Meridian): escalated to SRE and customer netops. Temporary workaround: tunnel apt/ yum traffic through bastion host (limited window) — documented in runbook patch 004.
- KV cache OOM (Horizon): suspected interaction between initial KV population and aggressive batching during ramp. Liam is reproducing on a smaller repro cluster to validate memory accounting.
- Observability gap: some preflight errors never surfaced as distinct alerts (they surfaced as generic package fetch errors). Need clearer alert taxonomy for preflight failures.

Decisions made this week:
- Add a 'preflight-networking' checklist item to explicitly verify split-horizon and mirror resolution for each customer site. (Owner: Maya). Deadline: 2027-04-22.
- Temporarily default worker concurrency lower for first 24h post-install in non-production installs to avoid KV warmup OOMs unless capacity testing passed. (Owner: Sofia).
- Add targeted metric: kv_cache_warmup_memory_bytes and alert if > 75% of node allocatable during warmup window. (Owner: Liam).

Open blockers (high priority):
- Meridian: DNS entries + egress rule changes pending from customer's netops. Customer timeline uncertain — risk: install delay > 2 weeks. (Owner: Ravi).
- Horizon: need a deterministic repro for the OOM pattern; until repro exists, only mitigations available. (Owner: Liam).

Action items (owners and timelines):
- Maya: patch private-deploy preflight doc with explicit mirror resolution checks + sample resolv.conf snippet. Due: 2027-04-22.
- Ravi: confirm Meridian netops contact and secure change window for static resolver entry. Due: 2027-04-20.
- Sofia: run controlled warmup test on staging with varied batch sizes and worker counts; capture memory profile. Due: 2027-04-21.
- Liam: create small repro job and open PR with instrumentation for kv cache accounting. Link PR to PD-3421. Due: 2027-04-23.
- Anya: align CS comms for Meridian customers, propose backup install windows and manage expectations. Due: 2027-04-19.

Notes to self / informal thread captures:
- Slack snippet: #pd-install -> "if we see package mirror fallback, try 10.0.5.8 resolver first" (Ravi). Need to formalize if used more than twice.
- Quick bench: warming KV with the mini-repro increased RSS by ~30% over baseline in the first 10 minutes — this correlates with the timing of the observed crashes.
- Observability ask: add a separate log tag for preflight validation failures (so we can filter them out of general package-failure noise).

Follow-ups for next weekly playback:
- Present initial KV warmup repro and proposed memory-capacity guardrails. (Liam + Sofia).
- Merge preflight doc patch and circulate to AE + CS for feedback. (Maya + Anya).
- If Meridian netops change window not confirmed, spin a remote-install fallback playbook and estimate manual effort. (Ravi).

Meeting cadence / logistics:
- Standing weekly playback: Mondays 09:30 PT. Next: 2027-04-25.
- Ad-hoc async updates in #pd-install for critical blockers (use 'pd-critical' tag to page SRE).

Appendix (links & quick refs):
- Confluence preflight (editable): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Private+Deploy+Preflight+Checklist
- Jira tickets referenced: PD-3421, PD-3487
- Current staging repro artifacts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/install-scripts/tree/staging/kv-repro

Quick retrospective note:
- Pattern: many installs reveal network and package mirror flakiness early — invest one sprint in a tighter preflight that simulates the exact resolver policies customers use (split-horizon, corporate proxies). This will save on-site engineer time.

End of playback.
